text:
erin: deploy-bot just bumped to minor for a tiny diagnostic change in metrics emitter. It only renames a metric label. Should be a patch, right?

release-bot: analysis: files touched: src/telemetry/metrics.rs, charts/observability.md -> heuristic: change in src -> candidate minor. Rule: default to minor for source edits. Override tokens accepted: [PATCH]/[MINOR].

nate: Renaming a label is backwards-compatible for consumers that use label names in dashboards -> actually could be breaking for customers. But 1) this is internal metric not exposed in public docs, 2) we have an automated migration mapping for dashboards. I'd still prefer patch with changelog callout.

lina: I'd vote for patch during the stable maintenance window. Minors trigger downstream dependency bumps and churn. If a change could theoretically break dashboards, we should coordinate a post-release note but not force semver bump.

erin: We're in the stable window until EOD Friday. Ops prefers minimal surface churn. I'll retitle the PR with [PATCH] and add a migration note under docs/observability.md.

devops-bot: quick note: tagging policy states any metric or telemetry rename that impacts external consumers must be minor. If internal only, prefer patch. We can't always determine "external" from CI heuristics.

nate: Could release-bot add a short checklist when it proposes a minor: "Does this affect external public API or exported metrics? Y/N" That would prompt human reviewers.

release-bot: enhancement queued: add 'affected-surface' prompt and a one-line rationale in the tag PR body. Manual override remains: `./tools/releasebot release --force-patch` or PR title token [PATCH].

lina: Also propose a soft-rule: during stable windows, prefer patch unless change adds capabilities or breaks API signatures. We'll add that to the release playbook.

erin: Retitled and forced patch: `v3.0.8` applied. Posting to #release-notes: "v3.0.8 (patch)  rename metric label (internal) + dashboard migration note".

nate: Tiny follow-up: can we pin the CLI helper in the release job so `--force-patch` requires an approval from release-approvers group? Prevent accidental mass patches?

release-bot: noted: flagged for policy RFC -> rfc/semver-stable-window#21. Adding annotation: "reason: src change but marked [PATCH] by author during stable window".

lina: Thanks — closing this thread. Will draft the playbook wording.
